# dsh-capability-composer
**The resident tool surface collapses into a few switchable sets, shrinking the system prompt on dem
resident tool surface collapses into a few switchable sets, shrinking the system prompt on demand.**
> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up upd
**DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.
> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** It occupies **one server-side seam (`system-prompt/assemble`)** —
only **4** plugins here share it — and its **two client slots are both `list` / `keyed`** (stackable
, one cell per key), never `chain`. See Compatibility.
**English** · 简体中文
**Shrink what the model sees, not what is running.**
## What this is
By default DSH stuffs all of the following **into every single request**:
| What gets stuffed in | Measured size |

| **Tool schema** registered by every installed plugin | 414 tool definitions / ~65.6K tokens |
| Th

e **catalog of all skills** | ~76K tokens as a baseline |
| The **system-prompt section** registered
by each plugin | `agent-teams:usage` ≈1296 tok + `plugin:dsh-docker` ≈579 tok + `plugin:api-client`
ugin | `agent-teams:usage` ≈1296 tok + `plugin:dsh-docker` ≈579 tok + `plugin:api-client` ≈254 tok |
Every request pays for "the things you might use", while only a few of them are actually useful in t
uest pays for "the things you might use", while only a few of them are actually useful in this turn.
`dsh-capability-composer` groups these into **compositions**, and **only lets the current compositio
n into the context**.
### What it does / what it does not do
Let's make the boundary clear first, because this is where misunderstandings happen most easily:
| ✅ It does | ❌ It does not |
| Narrow **the plugin catalog the model sees** | Never turns off any plugin — plugin processes keep

running, the UI keeps showing them |
| Shadow **skill catalog entries** that are not on the list | N

ever removes skills — `/skill-name` can still be invoked manually |
| Make tools **non-resident by d
efault** (keeping only the core + meta tools) | Does not restrict execution — `invoke_tool` can call

anything by default |
| Prune the **system-prompt sections** registered by plugins, according to th

e composition | Does not touch committed history |
| Resolve compositions at the session / workspace
/ global levels | Does not modify any third-party plugin file on disk |
In one sentence: **it shrinks "the catalog the model can see", not "the things that are running".**
Plugins keep running, skills stay available, tools stay callable — all that changes is how much gets
stuffed into each request.
## What it does (four mechanisms)
### ① Tools are non-resident by default
**Only 31 are resident**: the 28 official core tools, plus 3 meta tools — `search_plugins` / `load_p
lugin` / `invoke_tool`.
All other tools **never enter the tools list**. The model sees them in the catalog section of the sy
stem prompt (section heading `# 可用插件与 MCP 工具`), and calls them directly when needed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use `load_plugin` when a whole group needs to be loaded:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**The granularity is "plugin", not "tool name".** This is deliberate: finer granularity was tried —
after 417 / 211 tool names were compressed away, the model had no idea what to search for, which mad
e things harder to use instead. The granularity now is the plugin.
Mounting it prints one log line saying so:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### ② Skill shadowing (not disabling)
A skill that is not in the current skill composition gets a **shadow entry with the same name** regi
that is not in the current skill composition gets a **shadow entry with the same name** registered:
- `invocation.modelInvocable: false` — does not enter the skill catalog the model can see and auto-i

nvoke
- `rank: 0` — the lowest rank wins, shadowing the original skill
**`/skill-name` can still be invoked manually.**
One shadow entry is mounted at the global level, and every agent gets one more at the **"nearest lev
el"**, so that session-level compositions also take effect at the agent dimension.
### ③ Plugin compositions narrow "the model's plugin catalog"
Narrowing happens **when the catalog section is generated**, not by unloading plugins.
There are **two lines that are never narrowed**:
- **MCP server lines** — one line per MCP server; the tools inside a server are not governed by comp

ositions
- **The "unassigned tools" fallback line** — tools that cannot be attributed to any plugin
e "unassigned tools" fallback line** — tools that cannot be attributed to any plugin are always kept
### ④ System-prompt sections registered by plugins are pruned by composition too
[该节后续省略]
### Security

- **Anything non-loopback is 403** (`loopback only`)
- **A failed Origin check is always 403** (`ori
gin not allowed`) — local tools that send no Origin are let through
## Known limitations (stated plainly)
1. **Tool attribution is guessed by scanning source string literals; it is not an authoritative mapp
ing.** That is why `/state` carries three honest annotation fields: `exact` (exactly determined), `u

iOnly` (only used in the UI), `scanCertain` (scan confidence).
2. **The first scan of the plugin cat

alog takes about 5 seconds**; after that it goes through the `entry-id-map.json` cache.
3. **Auxilia
ry calls that do not pass `purpose`** are classified as the main route and are not affected by degra

dation.
4. **`GET` on `/state` has a side effect**: with `?_probeKeys=` it writes the reported real
keys into the auto section of `.composer-resident-tools` (it only writes the file; a restart applies
into the auto section of `.composer-resident-tools` (it only writes the file; a restart applies it).
